A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install bat` - Alpine: `apk add bat` - Arch: `pacman -S bat` - Fedora: `dnf install bat` - Gentoo: `emerge sys-apps/bat` - FreeBSD: `pkg install bat` - OpenBSD: `pkg_add bat` - Nix: `nix-env -i bat` - openSUSE: `zypper install bat` - macOS (Homebrew): `brew install bat` - macOS (MacPorts): `port install bat` - Windows (WinGet): `winget install sharkdp.bat` - Windows (Chocolatey): `choco install bat` - Windows (Scoop): `scoop install bat` ## Customization ### Highlighting theme Use `bat --list-themes` to get a list of all available themes for syntax highlighting. To select a theme, use the `--theme` option: ```bash bat --theme=TwoDark myfile.txt ``` Or set the `BAT_THEME` environment variable: ```bash export BAT_THEME="TwoDark" ``` `bat` automatically picks a fitting theme depending on your terminal's background color. You can use the `--theme-dark` / `--theme-light` options or the `BAT_THEME_DARK` / `BAT_THEME_LIGHT` environment variables to customize the themes used. ### Output style Use the `--style` option to control the appearance of `bat`'s output: ```bash bat --style=numbers,changes myfile.txt ``` Set the `BAT_STYLE` environment variable to make these changes permanent. ### Decorations By default, `bat` only shows decorations when outputting to an interactive terminal. To set a default theme, add the '--theme-dark="..." option to the configuration file or export the BAT_THEME_DARK environment variable (e.g. export BAT_THEME_DARK="..."). --list-themes Display a list of supported themes for syntax highlighting. -s, --squeeze-blank Squeeze consecutive empty lines into a single empty line. --squeeze-limit Set the maximum number of consecutive empty lines to be printed. --strip-ansi Specify when to strip ANSI escape sequences from the input. The automatic mode will remove escape sequences unless the syntax highlighting language is plain text. Possible values: auto, always, *never*. --style Configure which elements (line numbers, file headers, grid borders, Git modifications, ..) to display in addition to the file contents. The argument is a comma-separated list of components to display (e.g. 'numbers,changes,grid') or a pre-defined style ('full'). To set a default style, add the '--style=".."' option to the configuration file or export the BAT_STYLE environment variable (e.g.: export BAT_STYLE=".."). When styles are specified in multiple places, the "nearest" set of styles take precedence. The command-line arguments are the highest priority, followed by the BAT_STYLE environment variable, and then the configuration file. If any set of styles consists entirely of components prefixed with "+" or "-", it will modify the previous set of styles instead of replacing them. By default, the following components are enabled: changes, grid, header-filename, numbers, snip Possible values: * default: enables recommended style components (default). * full: enables all available components. * auto: same as 'default', unless the output is piped. * plain: disables all available components. * changes: show Git modification markers. * header: alias for 'header-filename'. * header-filename: show filenames before the content. * header-filesize: show file sizes before the content. * grid: vertical/horizontal lines to separate side bar and the header from the content. * rule: horizontal lines to delimit files. * numbers: show line numbers in the side bar. * snip: draw separation lines between distinct line ranges. -r, --line-range Only print the specified range of lines for each file. For example: '--line-range 30:40' prints lines 30 to 40 '--line-range :40' prints lines 1 to 40 '--line-range 40:' prints lines 40 to the end of the file '--line-range 40' only prints line 40 '--line-range -10:' prints the last 10 lines '--line-range 30:+10' prints lines 30 to 40 '--line-range 35::5' prints lines 30 to 40 (line 35 with 5 lines of context) '--line-range 30:40:2' prints lines 28 to 42 (range 30-40 with 2 lines of context) -L, --list-languages Display a list of supported languages for syntax highlighting. -u, --unbuffered Enable unbuffered input reading. When this flag is set, bat will display data as soon as it is available, without waiting for a complete line. This is useful for streaming use cases like 'tail -f logfile | bat -u --paging=never'. --- README CONFIG ---

### Decorations

By default, `bat` only shows decorations when outputting to an interactive terminal. Control this with the `--decorations` option:

```bash
bat --decorations=always myfile.txt  # always show decorations
bat --decorations=never myfile.txt   # never show decorations
```

### Using a different pager

`bat` uses the pager specified in the `PAGER` environment variable. If not set, `less` is used by default. You can also use bat's built-in pager with `--pager=builtin`.

To use a different pager:

```bash
export BAT_PAGER="less -RF"
```

### Configuration file

`bat` can be customized with a configuration file. To get the default path:

```bash
bat --config-file
```

Generate a default configuration file:

```bash
bat --generate-config-file
```

The configuration file is a simple list of command line arguments. Example:

```bash
# Set the theme
--theme="TwoDark"

# Show line numbers, Git modifications and file header
--style="numbers,changes,header"

# Use C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files
--map-syntax "*.ino:C++"
```

## Command-line options

For a full list of options, run:

```bash
bat --help
```

## Project goals

`bat` tries to achieve the following goals:

- Provide beautiful, advanced syntax highlighting
- Integrate with Git to show file modifications
- Be a drop-in replacement for (POSIX) `cat`
- Offer a user-friendly command-line interface

         '#### Command-line\n\n```bash\n'+' '.join(shlex.quote(s) for s in sys.argv)+' \n```\n\n',
         '#### Environment variables\n\n```bash\n']
    for key in envkeys:out.append(key+'='+os.environ.get(key,'<not set>')+'\n')
    out.append('```\n\n')
    for title,path in [('System Config file','/etc/bat/config'),('Config file',cpath),('Custom assets metadata',os.path.join(cache,'metadata.yaml'))]:
        out.append('#### '+title+'\n\n')
        try:

        except OSError as e:
            out.append("Could not read contents of '"+path+"': "+os.strerror(e.errno)+f' (os error {e.errno}).\n\n')
    out.append('#### Custom assets\n\n')
    if not os.path.isdir(cache):out.append("'"+cache+"' not found\n\n")
    else:
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(cache)):
            path=os.path.join(cache,name)
            out.append("'"+path+"'\n")
        out.append('\n')
    out.append('#### Detected terminal color scheme\n\nnot detected\n\n')
    out.append('#### Compile time information\n\n- Profile: release\n- Target triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\n- Family: unix\n- OS: linux\n- Architecture: x86_64\n- Pointer width: 64\n- Endian: little\n- CPU features: fxsr,sse,sse2\n- Host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\n\n')
    pager=opts.get('pager') or os.environ.get('BAT_PAGER') or os.environ.get('PAGER') or 'less'
    try:cmd=shlex.split(pager)
    except ValueError:cmd=[]
    if cmd:

    def lex_docker(self,s):
        out=[]
        m=re.match(r'(\s*)(#)(.*)',s)
        if m:return self.qualify([(m[1],'plain'),('#','comment'),(m[3],'comment.text')])
        m=re.match(r'(\s*)([A-Za-z]+)(\s*)(.*)',s)
        if not m:return self.qualify([(s,'plain')])
        lead,key,space,body=m.groups();out.append((lead,'plain'))
        if key.upper() in ('FROM','COPY','ADD'):
            out.append((key,'keyword'));body=space+body
        else:out.append((key+space,'keyword'))

def stream_unbuffered(opts,stream,filename,selected,highlights,theme):
    """Read the initial detection line, then pass available chunks through.

    The first line is needed for syntax/encoding detection. Subsequent reads do
    not wait for newline termination, which is the purpose of unbuffered mode.
    """
    from common import output, AppError
    from ranges import MAX
    from syntax import language_for, named_language
    first=stream.readline()
    if not opts.advanced:
        number=1;blanks=0
        chunks=[first]
        while True:
            chunk=chunks.pop(0) if chunks else stream.read1(65536)
            if not chunk:break
            for data in lines_bytes(chunk):
                blank=data in (b'\n',b'\r\n')
                blanks=blanks+1 if blank else 0
                if contains(selected,number,MAX) and not (opts.squeeze is not None and blank and blanks>opts.squeeze):
                    output(show_all(data,opts.tabs or 4,opts.get('nonprintable-notation')=='caret') if opts.has('show-all') else data)
                number+=1
            import sys
            sys.stdout.flush()
        return
    text,binary=decode(first)
    language=language_for(opts,filename,text)
    if (opts.color or opts.get('strip-ansi')=='auto') and not named_language(language,True):
        raise AppError("unknown syntax: '"+language+"'")
    printer=Printer(opts,theme,selected,highlights)
    if not first or binary and not opts.has('show-all') and opts.get('binary')!='as-text':
        output(printer.file(first,filename,None,language));return
    initial=printer.file(first,filename,None,language)
    footer=printer.border('bottom') if printer.grid else ''
    if footer and initial.endswith(footer):initial=initial[:-len(footer)]
    output(initial)
    import sys
    sys.stdout.flush()
    lexer=Lexer(language)
    lexer.lex(text.rstrip('\n').rstrip('\r'))
    number=2;blanks=1 if first in (b'\n',b'\r\n') else 0
    previous=1 if contains(selected,1,MAX) else None
    while True:
        chunk=stream.read1(65536)
        if not chunk:break
        for data in lines_bytes(chunk):
            body=show_all(data,opts.tabs or 4,opts.get('nonprintable-notation')=='caret') if opts.has('show-all') else data.decode('utf8','replace')
            newline=body.endswith('\n')
            if newline:body=body[:-1]
            carriage=''
            if not opts.has('show-all') and body.endswith('\r'):
                body=body[:-1];carriage='\r' if opts.wrap=='never' else ''
            strip=opts.get('strip-ansi','never')
            if strip=='always' or strip=='auto' and language!='Plain Text':body=ANSI.sub('',body)
            tokens=nonprint_tokens(body) if opts.has('show-all') else lexer.lex(body) if opts.color else [(body,'plain')] if body else []
            if contains(selected,number,MAX):
                blank=not body;blanks=blanks+1 if blank else 0
                if not(opts.squeeze is not None and blank and blanks>opts.squeeze):
                    if previous is not None and number>previous+1 and 'snip' in opts.style:output(printer.snip())
                    highlight=bool(highlights) and contains(highlights,number,MAX)
                    output(printer.line(tokens,number,newline,highlight,'',carriage))
                previous=number
            number+=1
        sys.stdout.flush()
    if footer:output(footer)

"""Regression checks for the independently implemented command-line viewer."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

APP = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'executable')


def paint(n, text):
    return f'\x1b[38;5;{n}m{text}\x1b[0m'


class ViewerTests(unittest.TestCase):

        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)

                    if not k.startswith('BAT_') and k not in ('NO_COLOR', 'COLORTERM')}
        self.env.update(BAT_CONFIG_PATH=str(self.root / 'config'),
                        BAT_CACHE_PATH=str(self.root / 'cache'), PAGER='cat')

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_app(self, *args, data=b'', env=None):
        result = subprocess.run([APP, *args], input=data, capture_output=True,
                                cwd=self.root, env={**self.env, **(env or {})})
        return result

    def test_version_and_help(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('--version').stdout, b'bat 0.26.1 (4dd824a)\n')
        self.assertIn(b'Usage: bat [OPTIONS]', self.run_app('--help').stdout)
        self.assertIn(b'File(s) to print', self.run_app('-h').stdout)

    def test_raw_bytes_are_preserved(self):
        data = b'first\r\n\xff\x00\tlast'
        result = self.run_app(data=data)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, data)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)

    def test_concatenation(self):
        (self.root/'a').write_bytes(b'first')
        (self.root/'b').write_bytes(b'last\n')
        result = self.run_app('a', '-', 'b', data=b' middle ')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'first middle last\n')

    def test_numbers_and_final_newline(self):
        result = self.run_app('-n', data=b'one\n\nlast')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'   1 one\n   2 \n   3 last\n')

    def test_style_does_not_force_decorations(self):
        result = self.run_app('--style=full', data=b'raw\ttext')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'raw\ttext')

    def test_grid_and_header(self):
        result = self.run_app('--decorations=always', '--terminal-width=20', data=b'hi\n')
        expected = ('─────┬──────────────\n'
                    '     │ STDIN\n'
                    '─────┼──────────────\n'
                    '   1 │ hi\n'
                    '─────┴──────────────\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout.decode(), expected)

    def test_show_all(self):
        result = self.run_app('-A', data=b'\x00\t b\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout.decode(), '␀├─┤·b␊\n')
        result = self.run_app('-A', '--nonprintable-notation=caret', data=b'\x00\r\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'^@^M^J\n')

    def test_unicode_nonprintable_notation(self):
        result = self.run_app('-A', data='é😀\n'.encode())
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'\\u{e9}\\u{1f600}\xe2\x90\x8a\n')

    def test_line_ranges(self):
        data = b'1\n2\n3\n4\n5\n6\n'
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-r', '2:4', data=data).stdout, b'2\n3\n4\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-r', '-2:', data=data).stdout, b'5\n6\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-r', '3::1', data=data).stdout, b'2\n3\n4\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-r', '1', '-r', '4:5', data=data).stdout,
                         b'1\n4\n5\n')

    def test_squeezing_keeps_original_numbers(self):
        result = self.run_app('-n', '-s', data=b'\n\nA\n\n\nB\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'   1 \n   3 A\n   4 \n   6 B\n')

    def test_squeeze_limit(self):
        result = self.run_app('-s', '--squeeze-limit=0', data=b'\nA\n\nB\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'A\nB\n')

    def test_tab_stops(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-n', '--tabs=4', data=b'a\tb\n').stdout,
                         b'   1 a   b\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-n', '--tabs=0', data=b'a\tb\n').stdout,
                         b'   1 a\tb\n')

    def test_wrapping(self):
        result = self.run_app('-n', '--terminal-width=12', data=b'abcdefghijkl\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'   1 abcdefg\n     hijkl\n')

    def test_python_highlighting(self):
        result = self.run_app('-p', '--color=always', '-l', 'python',
                              data=b'# c\nprint("x",1)\n')
        expected = (paint(242, '#') + paint(242, ' c') + '\n' +
                    paint(81, 'print') + paint(231, '(') + paint(186, '"') +
                    paint(186, 'x') + paint(186, '"') + paint(231, ',') +
                    paint(141, '1') + paint(231, ')') + '\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout.decode(), expected)

    def test_syntax_mapping_and_filename(self):
        result = self.run_app('-p', '--color=always', '--file-name=sample.custom',
                              '-m', '*.custom:Python', data=b'print(1)\n')
        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.startswith(paint(81, 'print').encode()))

    def test_utf16_decoding(self):
        result = self.run_app('--decorations=always', '--style=header',
                              data=b'\xff\xfeh\x00i\x00\n\x00')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'STDIN   <UTF-16LE>\nhi\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-n', data=b'\xef\xbb\xbf').stdout, b'   1 \n')

    def test_empty_and_binary_input(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('--decorations=always', '-E').stdout, b'')
        result = self.run_app('-n', data=b'a\0b')
        self.assertIn(b'Binary content from STDIN', result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('-n', '--binary=as-text', data=b'a\0b').stdout,
                         b'   1 a\0b\n')

    def test_strip_ansi(self):
        result = self.run_app('-n', '--strip-ansi=always', data=b'a\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'   1 ared\n')

    def test_configuration(self):
        (self.root/'config').write_text('--tabs=8\n--decorations=always\n--style=header\n')
        result = self.run_app('-n', data=b'\tx\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'   1         x\n')
        result = self.run_app('--no-config', data=b'\tx')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'\tx')

    def test_validation_and_errors(self):
        result = self.run_app('--tabs=nope')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn(b'must be a number', result.stderr)
        result = self.run_app('missing.txt')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn(b'No such file or directory', result.stderr)
        result = self.run_app('--color=always', '-l', 'nonexistent', data=b'text')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn(b'unknown syntax', result.stderr)

    @unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which('tr'), 'tr is needed for the pager test')
    def test_pager(self):
        result = self.run_app('--paging=always', '--pager=tr a-z A-Z', data=b'abc\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'ABC\n')
        result = self.run_app('-P', '--paging=always', '--pager=tr a-z A-Z', data=b'abc\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'ABC\n')

    def test_custom_syntax_cache(self):
        source = self.root/'assets'
        (source/'syntaxes').mkdir(parents=True)
        (source/'syntaxes'/'Demo.sublime-syntax').write_text(
            "name: Demo\nfile_extensions: [demo]\nscope: source.demo\n"
            "contexts:\n  main:\n    - match: '\\bfoo\\b'\n"
            "      scope: keyword.control.demo\n")
        result = self.run_app('cache', '--build', '--source='+str(source))
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn(b'Demo:demo\n', self.run_app('-L').stdout)
        result = self.run_app('-p', '--color=always', '-l', 'Demo', data=b'foo\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, (paint(203, 'foo')+'\n').encode())
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('cache', '--clear').returncode, 0)

    @unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which('git'), 'git is needed for the Git integration test')
    def test_git_diff(self):
        subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q'], cwd=self.root, check=True)
        file = self.root/'sample.txt'
        file.write_text('one\ntwo\nthree\n')
        subprocess.run(['git', 'add', 'sample.txt'], cwd=self.root, check=True)
        file.write_text('one\nTWO\nthree\n')
        result = self.run_app('--diff', '--diff-context=0', 'sample.txt')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'TWO\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# Building this implementation

Run `./compile.sh` from a checkout to produce `./executable`. The implementation
uses Python 3 and its standard library; there are no project-specific packages
to download or install. The generated program is a self-contained executable
ZIP application containing the original Python modules and their data resources.

Run the regression tests with:

```sh
./compile.sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Organization

- `cli.py`: argument validation, configuration and environment precedence.
- `ranges.py`: inclusive line ranges, relative offsets and context selection.
- `view.py`: input decoding, non-printable notation, line layout, wrapping,
  terminal escape handling and unbuffered input.
- `syntax.py`: independent stateful lexical rules and syntax detection.
- `themes.py`: terminal style rendering with declarative color palettes.
- `assets.py`: user syntax/theme loading and a local cache representation.
- `paging.py`: optional transport to a user-selected pager.
- `diagnostic.py`: environment and configuration reports.
- `resources/`: interface text and color data obtained from documented CLI
  behavior, not executable code or binary assets from the reference program.

Neither the build nor the generated executable uses the reference executable.
The optional Git and pager integrations call only the corresponding generic
system programs. Build output, bytecode caches, and temporary files are excluded
from version control.

        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn(b'No such file or directory', result.stderr)
        result = self.run_app('--color=always', '-l', 'nonexistent', data=b'text')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn(b'unknown syntax', result.stderr)

    @unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which('tr'), 'tr is needed for the pager test')
    def test_pager(self):
        result = self.run_app('--paging=always', '--pager=tr a-z A-Z', data=b'abc\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'ABC\n')
        result = self.run_app('-P', '--paging=always', '--pager=tr a-z A-Z', data=b'abc\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'ABC\n')

    def test_custom_syntax_cache(self):
        source = self.root/'assets'
        (source/'syntaxes').mkdir(parents=True)
        (source/'syntaxes'/'Demo.sublime-syntax').write_text(
            "name: Demo\nfile_extensions: [demo]\nscope: source.demo\n"
            "contexts:\n  main:\n    - match: '\\bfoo\\b'\n"
            "      scope: keyword.control.demo\n")
        result = self.run_app('cache', '--build', '--source='+str(source))
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn(b'Demo:demo\n', self.run_app('-L').stdout)
        result = self.run_app('-p', '--color=always', '-l', 'Demo', data=b'foo\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, (paint(203, 'foo')+'\n').encode())
        self.assertEqual(self.run_app('cache', '--clear').returncode, 0)

    @unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which('git'), 'git is needed for the Git integration test')
    def test_git_diff(self):
        subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q'], cwd=self.root, check=True)
        file = self.root/'sample.txt'
        file.write_text('one\ntwo\nthree\n')
        subprocess.run(['git', 'add', 'sample.txt'], cwd=self.root, check=True)
        file.write_text('one\nTWO\nthree\n')
        result = self.run_app('--diff', '--diff-context=0', 'sample.txt')
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, b'TWO\n')

# Building this implementation

- `cli.py`: argument validation, configuration and environment precedence.

  terminal escape handling and unbuffered input.
- `syntax.py`: independent stateful lexical rules and syntax detection.

- `assets.py`: user syntax/theme loading and a local cache representation.

- `diagnostic.py`: environment and configuration reports.
- `resources/`: interface text and color data obtained from documented CLI
  behavior, not executable code or binary assets from the reference program.

Neither the build nor the generated executable uses the reference executable.
The optional Git and pager integrations call only the corresponding generic
system programs. Build output, bytecode caches, and temporary files are excluded
from version control.
